content: The following individuals contributed to the development of the guidelines for tuberculosis (TB) treatment and management, particularly focusing on drug-resistant TB (DR-TB): 1. Pulmonary Medicine and Tuberculosis Experts: Dr. Lisa Chen, a clinician and academic affiliated with the UCSF Curry International Tuberculosis Center in the USA. Dr. Farhana Amanullah, a pediatrician and pediatric nephrologist from Interactive Research and Development in Pakistan. Dr. Mathilde Jachym, a pulmonologist working at a sanatorium in France. 2. Clinicians and End Users: Dr. Anna Marie Celine Garfin, a clinician from the National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) in the Philippines. Dr. Edwin H. Herrera-Flores, a clinician at the Hospital Nacional MDR-TB Referral Centre in Lima, Peru. Dr. Bhavana Shrestha, a clinician from the Nepal Anti-TB Association in Nepal. Dr. Ivan Solovic, a clinician from the National Institute for TB, Lung Diseases, and Thoracic Surgery in Slovakia. Dr. Carlos Torres, a clinician and technical expert from the Latin American Thoracic Society in Colombia. Dr. Zarir Udwadia, a clinician from the Hinduja Hospital MDR-TB Referral Centre in Mumbai, India. 3. Civil Society Representatives and Former MDR-TB Patients: Mildred Fernando-Pancho from the Philippines. Thato Mosidi from South Africa. 4. Technical Agencies and Researchers: Dr. Guy Marks, a clinician and researcher from the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in Australia. Dr. Sarabjit Singh Chadha, a technical expert from the Global Drug Initiative Working Group in India. 5. Epidemiologists and Biostatisticians: Dr. Lawrence Mbuagbaw, an epidemiologist and biostatistician from McMaster University in Canada. 6. Observers and External Partners: Dr. Draurio Barreira Cravo Neto, a technical manager for TB at Unitaid in Switzerland. Dr. Dan Everitt, Vice President and Senior Medical Officer at the TB Alliance in the USA. Dr. Christopher Gilpin, a global laboratory coordinator at the International Organization for Migration in Switzerland. Dr. Blessi Kumar, a civil society representative from the Global Coalition of TB Activists in India. 7. WHO Steering Committee Members: Dr. Fuad Mirzayev (lead), Dr. Dennis Falzon, Dr. Medea Gegia, Dr. Ernesto Jaramillo, Dr. Alexei Korobitsyn, Dr. Linh Nguyen, Dr. Kerri Viney, and Dr. Matteo Zignol from the WHO Global Tuberculosis Programme. Dr. Corinne Simone Collette Merle from the WHO Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases. Dr. Lorenzo Moja from the WHO Medicines Selection, Intellectual Property, and Affordability Programme. Dr. Andreas Alois Reis from WHO Health Ethics and Governance. Dr. Satvinder (Vindi) Singh from the WHO Global HIV, Hepatitis, and STIs Programmes. 8. Evidence Reviewers: Dr. Richard Menzies, the lead evidence reviewer from McGill University’s Faculty of Medicine in Canada. Dr. Jonathon R. Campbell, an epidemiologist and health economist from McGill University. Dr. Amrita Daftary, a behavioral health scientist from York University in Canada. Dr. Gabriela Gomez, a health economist from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine in the UK. Dr. Emily Ann Kendall, an assistant professor of medicine at Johns Hopkins University in the USA. Dr. Stephanie Law, a qualitative researcher from McGill University. Dr. Rada Savic, an expert in bioengineering and pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics from the University of California, San Francisco. Dr. Nicholas Winters, a research assistant from McGill University. 9. Definitions and Key Concepts: Bacteriologically Confirmed TB: Diagnosed when a biological specimen tests positive for TB through smear microscopy, culture, or a rapid diagnostic test recommended by WHO. Clinically Diagnosed TB: Diagnosed by a medical practitioner based on clinical judgment when bacteriological confirmation is not available. Drug-Resistant TB (DR-TB): Caused by strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistant to one or more TB medications. Extensively Drug-Resistant TB (XDR-TB): Caused by strains resistant to rifampicin, fluoroquinolones, and at least one Group A drug (bedaquiline or linezolid). Multidrug-Resistant TB (MDR-TB): Caused by strains resistant to both rifampicin and isoniazid. Pre-Extensively Drug-Resistant TB (Pre-XDR-TB): Caused by strains resistant to rifampicin and at least one fluoroquinolone. Rifampicin-Resistant TB (RR-TB): Caused by strains resistant to rifampicin. Severe Extrapulmonary TB: Includes miliary TB, TB meningitis, osteoarticular TB, or pericardial TB. 10. WHO Consolidated Guidelines: The guidelines focus on evidence-based recommendations for the treatment and care of patients with DR-TB, including shorter all-oral regimens and monitoring of patient responses. The recommendations are based on the GRADE approach, which evaluates evidence to formulate policy recommendations. Recent updates include the use of bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, and moxifloxacin (BPaLM regimen) and 9-month all-oral regimens for MDR/RR-TB. These guidelines aim to improve the management of DR-TB and support national TB programs in implementing effective treatment strategies.
